(S)-dimetindene, the (S)-(4-F-methyl)carbamate analogue of McN-A-343, the quaternary compound BN 228 and the (S)-isomers of 4-F- and 3-F-methylpyridiniumcarbamates are the most selective muscarinic ligands known today.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the development of selective M1 agonists and M2 antagonists is possible and that such agents could be useful tools to study the role of muscarinic receptors in the treatment of CNS disorders.
the development of new selective muscarinic ligands is still possible.
the chiral C1-methyl substitution is a powerful strategy for the design of selective muscarinic agents with high potency and good pharmacological properties.
